name: VoiceStudio
tagline: A free, local alternative to ElevenLabs: clone voices, dub videos, and make audiobooks in 646 languages without sending your data anywhere
sentence: A desktop app that runs entirely on your own computer - clone a voice from a 3-second clip, dub videos into other languages, transcribe audio, or create full audiobooks, all without a subscription or cloud account.

board.say: Voice cloning and video dubbing tools charge per character, cap your usage, and send your audio to someone else's servers.
board.eg: ElevenLabs starts at $5/month, limits your characters, and processes everything in the cloud.

board.say: You give it a short audio clip of a voice (3 seconds is enough), a video file, or text for an audiobook.
board.eg: Record 3 seconds of your voice into your microphone, or drop in a video you want dubbed into Spanish.

board.say: It runs AI models on your own hardware - clones the voice, translates and re-speaks video dialogue, or generates a full audiobook with chapter markers.
board.eg: It isolates the voice from background noise, translates the script, and re-speaks it in the cloned voice with synchronized timing.

board.say: You get cloned voice files, dubbed videos, or complete audiobooks - all made locally, with nothing sent to the cloud.
board.eg: A 30-minute video dubbed into 3 languages, or a full audiobook in .m4b format with chapters, all from your laptop.

before: Voice cloning and dubbing services charge per character and require sending your audio to the cloud.
Making an audiobook means hiring a narrator or paying a voice-AI subscription - both cost hundreds.
If you need dubbing in multiple languages, each one multiplies the cost and the wait.
after: Clone any voice from a **3-second clip** and use it as much as you want - no per-character fees, no subscription.
Dub a video into any of **646 languages** and the tool matches the timing of the original dialogue automatically.
Create a full audiobook with chapter markers from a PDF or EPUB - on your own machine, with nothing leaving your computer.
uses_note: About 6 months old and growing fast. Most users are content creators, language learners, and accessibility advocates.

uses.what: Wrote a viral thread on X about VoiceStudio, testing voice cloning from a 3-second clip and comparing it to ElevenLabs.
uses.result: Concluded: "ElevenLabs still wins on polish, VoiceStudio wins on price, privacy, and reach."

uses.what: Shared VoiceStudio with his DevOps audience on X, calling it the open-source ElevenLabs alternative.
uses.result: Highlighted voice cloning, dubbing, transcription and audiobook creation in one app.

uses.what: Users running audiobook jobs on consumer hardware, using multi-GPU setups, and cloning voices across languages.
uses.result: The issue tracker shows real-world usage at scale: GPU memory problems, audiobook timeout bugs, and multi-language dubbing requests.

steps: Download the installer for your system from the Releases page (DMG for Mac, MSI for Windows, AppImage for Linux), or run `curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh`.
Open the app, go to the Voice Cloning workspace, record or upload 3 seconds of your voice, type a sentence, and click Generate.
Try video dubbing: drop a video file into the Dubbing workspace, pick a target language, and let it dub.

best_for: You want to clone a voice or dub a video without paying per character or sending audio to the cloud
You create content in multiple languages and need affordable dubbing
You want to make an audiobook from a PDF without hiring a narrator
skip_if: You need the absolute best voice quality - ElevenLabs still wins on polish and naturalness
You have a Mac with an Intel chip - only Apple Silicon is supported natively
You want to use the cloned voices commercially - the default AI model's license does not allow commercial use without swapping to a different model

alternatives.name: ElevenLabs
alternatives.line: The commercial leader. Cloud-based, subscription pricing, 32 languages. Best-in-class voice quality. Starts at $5/month.

alternatives.name: Bark (by Suno)
alternatives.line: Open-source text-to-audio model that can generate speech, music and sound effects. MIT license. More of a raw model than a full app.

watch: **The default voice model blocks commercial use.** The software is AGPL-3.0 (commercial OK if you share source), but the default voice model carries a CC-BY-NC license. Commercial voice generation requires swapping to a different model.
**GPU hungry.** Minimum 4 GB of video memory, recommended 8 GB+. Users with 6-8 GB GPUs report hitting memory barriers. CPU-only mode works but is much slower.

**Early-stage stability.** v0.5.x with 2,300+ issues filed in 5 months. The project recently migrated its desktop framework (from Tauri to Electron), which suggests the architecture is still settling.
